Package common.core.fsm

package common.core.fsm
State machines: subsystems that are always in one named state and only change state in ways you've allowed.

Why use one

A subsystem like an intake does a few distinct things: sit still, pull game pieces in, spit them out. Writing those as states (NEUTRAL, INTAKE, OUTTAKE) makes the robot's behavior easy to read, easy to show on a dashboard, and hard to get into a bad combination, since a request for a move you haven't allowed is ignored.

The pieces

  • FSMSubsystemBase: the subsystem. Extend it, list your states in an enum, and call setState(...) to change state.
  • Transition: one allowed move, from one state to another, and the command that does it.
  • TransitionMap: every allowed move. It has shortcuts for adding many at once, like "from any state to NEUTRAL".

A state machine can also control other state machines. The robot's Superstructure, for example, has states like SHOOT that set the intake's, hopper's and shooter's states together.
